event: Complex societies and urban centers develop in parts of the Iranian plateau; local chronologies vary.
Elamite, Median, Persian, and neighboring political formations interact across the plateau and Mesopotamia.
Cyrus II defeats the Median ruler and expands the Persian polity.
Cyrus II captures Babylon; the Cyrus Cylinder is associated with the new regime's Babylonian royal legitimation.
Alexander's conquest ends Achaemenid imperial rule.
Ardashir I establishes Sasanian rule after defeating the last Arsacid king.
Arab-Muslim conquests end the Sasanian state; religious and cultural transformations continue over generations.
Safavid rule begins under Shah Ismail I; the dynasty promotes Twelver Shi'ism as a central state institution.
Constitutional Revolution challenges arbitrary rule and establishes constitutional institutions amid conflict and foreign pressure.
The Pahlavi dynasty begins after the end of Qajar rule.
Iran nationalizes its oil industry; Mohammad Mosaddeq becomes prime minister.
A coup overthrows Mosaddeq's government; declassified U.S. records document U.S. intelligence involvement.
The monarchy falls in a revolution and the Islamic Republic is established through a new constitutional order.
Iran and Iraq fight a prolonged war with major consequences for both societies.
Iran and the E3/EU+3 conclude the JCPOA; UN Security Council Resolution 2231 endorses it.
The UN Security Council page records a change in the status of earlier Iran-related resolutions effective 27 September 2025; verify current legal records.
